correctness.rationale: A three-object acyclic nerve without a composable pair is a graph, hence cannot have the required torsion H1. After labeling the chain 0<1<2, its counts are 3 vertices, a+b+c edges and ab triangles, so χ=1 gives m=ab+2. Removing the sink leaves a graph Y with a parallel arrows. The sink link Γ has g- and h-vertices, an edge per pair g∘f=h, and a map to Y sending that edge to f. The cone attaches one new vertex, one spoke per sink arrow, and exactly the composable triangles, giving the nerve. Its reduced homology sequence surjects H1(B C) onto the free group H̃0(Γ); finite H1 forces Γ connected. Then H1(B C) is a quotient of Z^(a−1), so reducing mod 2 gives a−1≥r. Reversal of simplices for the opposite category gives b−1≥r. Equality in m≥(r+1)²+2 fixes a=b=r+1, c=r²+1; reversing the two equal adjacent sizes does not change this triple. In the constructed graph the r squares meet along one edge and all other edges are leaves. A spanning tree is obtained by deleting one nonshared edge per square; hence these squares are a free loop basis. The map to Y reads f0⁻¹ f_i f0⁻¹ f_i on the i-th square. Contracting f0 in Y, the cone attaches one 2-cell along the square of each separate basis element. The resulting wedge of degree-two cones is the required wedge of real projective planes, not just a space with matching homology. The argument includes r=1, without claiming priority there.
residual_risks: The finite Smith checks corroborate only the construction and not the homotopy-type assertion or the universal bound; both follow separately from the cone proof.

value.rationale: A sharp quadratic resource cost at the least possible object count is a natural invariant for categorical models. The result forces two separate dimensions of every optimal table and realizes them in a model with the specified homotopy type. This is useful beyond isolated small-count checks, and the two-sided torsion bound addresses a gap not answered by general existence.
residual_risks: The invariant neither classifies optimal categories up to isomorphism nor minimizes over unrestricted object counts.
